**Issue #4141 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4141: Patch: the moderate levers write their bans, revocations and redemption pauses to the admin audit
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Today banning an account, unbanning one, revoking an invite code, or pausing invite redemption leaves its only trace in the terminal where the command ran. If that scrollback is lost, nobody can later answer "who banned this account, and when?" Every smaller dev power already writes a row the dev dashboard's Audit page shows: granting XP, filling a collection, hand-setting a rating. After this change the four big levers do too. Each ban, unban, revocation and pause or resume appears on the same Audit page with what was asked and the state before and after, for example a ban row naming the account with `active` before and `banned` after.

## Why

- These levers are the strongest in the system: they shut players out and gate entry for everyone. They deserve at least the record a dev XP grant already gets (R3074000).
- Two code facts pin the gap: `cli/moderate.rs` says "Stdout is the audit trail", while `admin_actions_append` refuses anything that is not an `/api/dev` or `/api/admin` route (`check_route` in `admin/store.rs`), and migration 0080's `admin_actions_route_check` says the same in SQL. So even a willing caller cannot record a lever run today.
- The table already fits lever rows: `profile_id` is nullable (`on delete set null`), and `Audit.tsx` renders route, request, before and after as generic text, so the dashboard shows the new rows with no admin change.

## Proposal

- Each lever run writes one `admin_actions` row in the same transaction as the change it makes: ban and unban (the account, old status into new), revoke-code (the stored code hash, never the plaintext), redemption on and off (old state into new). The actor `profile_id` is NULL: the CLI runs as the operator and holds no profile; the route names the lever (for example `CLI moderate ban`).
- A lever that changes nothing writes nothing: `already banned`, an unknown profile or code, and a refused unban of a pending account keep today's stdout line and add no row, matching how refused dev routes write nothing.
- Widen the route guard in both places it lives: `check_route` in `admin/store.rs` gains the explicit lever names (an allow-list, not a loose prefix), and a new migration widens `admin_actions_route_check` the same way, since 0080 is checksum-pinned.
- Update the `moderate.rs` header comment, which today promises stdout as the audit trail, to name both records.
- No ruling note: this is operational record-keeping, like `alerts.rs`, which carries no R-row.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/migrations/0095_moderation_audit.sql` (0094 is the newest today): the widened route check.
- `crates/server/src/admin/store.rs`: `check_route` and a small constructor for lever rows reusing `admin_actions_append` (which already dispatches to the Postgres and fake stores together).
- `crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs`: one append beside each of the four writes, inside its transaction.
- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` and `crates/server/tests/store/moderate.rs`: fake and Postgres parity plus per-lever cases; `migrations_pinned.rs` gains the new file's line.
- No `apps/admin` change: the Audit page renders the rows as they stand. SPEC needs no change (SPEC §9.4 names the levers, §14.10 and R3074000 name the audit; neither's rule changes).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ban`, `unban`, `revoke-code` and `redemption on|off` each write exactly one `admin_actions` row with the correct before and after when they change something, in the same transaction as the change.
- [ ] No-ops and refusals (`already banned`, unknown profile or code, pending unban) write no row and print today's stdout line unchanged.
- [ ] The rows are visible through `GET /api/admin/audit` as a dev account and on the dashboard's Audit page with no admin code change.
- [ ] No row ever carries an invite code in plaintext, only the stored hash.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and the `sql` suite (pinned checksums) pass.

## Size and risks

Medium: one migration, one small store addition, four call sites, and contract plus CLI tests. The main risk is the widened route check: keep it an explicit list of lever names so no other writer can smuggle rows in. The rejected alternative was a second audit table for CLI runs: it would need its own dashboard read path and trust-boundary review, while this table already has both. A decision the task left open: the operator is recorded as NULL rather than a named identity, because only holders of `DATABASE_URL` and `CODE_PEPPER` can run these commands, so who reduces to who holds the production environment, as today.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44219872594)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

After this change, `moderate ban`, `unban`, `revoke-code` and `redemption on|off` each write exactly one `admin_actions` row in the same transaction as the change they make, with actor `profile_id` NULL and a lever route name; no-ops and refusals (`already banned`, unknown profile or code, refused pending unban) write no row and keep today's stdout line. The route guard is widened to the explicit lever names in both `check_route` (`crates/server/src/admin/store.rs`) and a new migration, so `GET /api/admin/audit` and the dashboard Audit page show the rows with no admin code change. No spec rule and no ruling changes.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/migrations/0095_moderation_audit.sql` | new | Widens `admin_actions_route_check` to the four lever routes; re-appliable header/style like `0094` |
| `crates/server/src/admin/store.rs` | change | `NewAdminAction.profile_id` becomes `Option<String>`; new `MODERATE_AUDIT_ROUTES` consts plus `NewAdminAction::moderate` constructor; `check_route` allow-list; `pg::actions_append` and `fake::actions_append` NULL handling |
| `crates/server/src/api/admin.rs` | change | `audit()` wraps the caller id in `Some` for the new `Option` field (one line) |
| `crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs` | change | One `admin_actions_append` beside each of the four writes, inside its transaction; header comment names both records |
| `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` | change | New `mod moderate_audit` with `both_stores!` parity cases for lever rows |
| `crates/server/tests/store/moderate.rs` | change | Per-lever row and no-row assertions in the existing `moderate_commands` tests |
| `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` | change | One new PINNED line for `0095_moderation_audit.sql` with its checksum |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `apps/admin`, or anything under `spec/`. Governing spec: §9.4 (the levers), §14.10 and R3074000 (the audit); neither rule changes, so no ruling note and no `spec/pending/` paragraph (like `alerts.rs`, which carries no R-row).

## Steps

1. `crates/server/src/admin/store.rs`, struct `NewAdminAction`: change field `profile_id: String` to `profile_id: Option<String>`, keeping `route`, `request`, `before`, `after`, `at` as-is. Update its doc comment to say `None` is the CLI operator, which holds no profile.
2. Same file, new constants and constructor next to `NewAdminAction`: add `pub const MODERATE_AUDIT_BAN_ROUTE: &str = "CLI moderate ban";` and likewise `..._UNBAN_ROUTE = "CLI moderate unban"`, `..._REVOKE_ROUTE = "CLI moderate revoke-code"`, `..._REDEMPTION_ROUTE = "CLI moderate redemption"`, plus `pub const MODERATE_AUDIT_ROUTES: &[&str]` listing all four. Add `impl NewAdminAction { pub fn moderate(route: &'static str, request: Value, before: Value, after: Value, at: i64) -> Self }` with `profile_id: None`; assert via `debug_assert!(MODERATE_AUDIT_ROUTES.contains(&route))`. Copy the `json!` value style from `api/admin.rs`.
3. Same file, `check_route`: keep the existing method/path check unchanged, and accept `MODERATE_AUDIT_ROUTES.contains(&route)` as an additional `||` branch. Refuse everything else exactly as today with the same `"no dev or admin route"` message.
4. Same file, `pg::actions_append`: change `run_as(t, Some(action.profile_id.as_str()))` to `run_as(t, action.profile_id.as_deref())` and keep `.bind(&action.profile_id)` (now `Option<String>`, so `None` inserts NULL under `$1::uuid`). `fake::actions_append`: change `profile_id: Some(action.profile_id.clone())` to `profile_id: action.profile_id.clone()`.
5. `crates/server/src/api/admin.rs`, `audit()`: change `profile_id: profile_id.to_string()` to `profile_id: Some(profile_id.to_string())`. Nothing else in this file changes; `get_audit` already maps `None` to `""`.
6. `crates/server/migrations/0095_moderation_audit.sql` (new): copy the header-comment style of `0094` (purpose, trust boundary, apply order `... -> 0094 -> 0095`, safe to re-apply). Body: `alter table public.admin_actions drop constraint if exists admin_actions_route_check;` then `add constraint admin_actions_route_check check (route ~ '^(GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) /api/(dev|admin)/' or route in ('CLI moderate ban', 'CLI moderate unban', 'CLI moderate revoke-code', 'CLI moderate redemption'));`. Same constraint name, no other table touched.
7. `crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs`, `ban_profile`: after `profiles_set_status(.., Banned)` and before `tx.commit()`, append `tx.admin_actions_append(&NewAdminAction::moderate(MODERATE_AUDIT_BAN_ROUTE, json!({"profileId": profile_id}), json!({"status": before_status}), json!({"status": "banned"}), now_ms())).await.map_err(|error| anyhow!("{error}"))?;` where `before_status` is the `profile.status` read at the top (`"pending"` or `"active"` as its `as_str`). The `already banned` early return and the unknown-profile `bail!` stay untouched and write nothing. Add imports `crate::admin::store::{MODERATE_AUDIT_BAN_ROUTE, NewAdminAction}`, `crate::app::now_ms`, `serde_json::json`.
8. Same file, `unban_profile`: after `profiles_set_status(.., Active)` and before `commit`, append with `MODERATE_AUDIT_UNBAN_ROUTE`, request `{"profileId": profile_id}`, before `{"status": "banned"}`, after `{"status": "active"}`. The pending `bail!`, the `already active` return and the unknown-profile `bail!` stay untouched.
9. Same file, `revoke_code`: after `let revoked = tx.codes_revoke_by_hash(&hash).await?;`, append only when `revoked` is true, with `MODERATE_AUDIT_REVOKE_ROUTE`, request `json!({"codeHash": hash})` (the stored hash, never the plaintext `plain` or `canonical`), before `{"revoked": false}`, after `{"revoked": true}`. The `already revoked` branch keeps its commit and writes nothing; malformed/unknown `bail!`s stay as-is.
10. Same file, `set_redemption`: after `let previous = tx.redemption_set_enabled(enabled).await?;`, append only when `previous != enabled`, with `MODERATE_AUDIT_REDEMPTION_ROUTE`, request `json!({"enabled": enabled})`, before `json!({"enabled": previous})`, after `json!({"enabled": enabled})`. The `already paused`/`already resumed` lines stay untouched.
11. Same file, module doc comment (lines 17–19): replace `Stdout is the audit trail: the CLI has no log pipeline, so the line it prints is the record.` with `The line it prints and the admin_actions row it writes in the same transaction are the record: stdout for the operator, the row (actor NULL, a CLI moderate route) for the dashboard Audit page.`
12. `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, helper `action()`: change `profile_id: profile_id.to_string()` to `Some(...)`. Add `mod moderate_audit` after `mod dev_dashboard`: `both_stores!(moderate_lever_routes_round_trip_with_null_actor, moderate_route_guard_stays_an_allow_list);`. First case: append one row per lever route with `profile_id: None` (build via `NewAdminAction::moderate`), assert `actions_recent` returns them newest-first with `profile_id: None` and exact request/before/after, and that `profiles_remove` of an unrelated account keeps them. Second case: assert the four lever routes append `Ok`, and near-misses (`"CLI moderate ban "`, `"cli moderate ban"`, `"CLI moderate"`, `"CLI moderate ban extra"`, `"POST /api/devtools/x"`) are `Err`.
13. `crates/server/tests/store/moderate.rs`: in each existing success test, open a transaction after the lever runs, call `admin_actions_recent(10)`, and assert exactly one new row with the expected route, `profile_id: None`, and JSON: ban `{"profileId": id}` / `{"status": <prior>}` / `{"status": "banned"}`; unban `{"status": "banned"}` / `{"status": "active"}`; revoke `{"codeHash": <hash>}` with `{"revoked": false}` / `{"revoked": true}` plus `assert!(!row text contains plaintext)`; redemption `{"enabled": previous}` / `{"enabled": enabled}`. In each no-op test (`already banned`, `already active`, `already revoked`, `already paused/resumed`, unknown profile/code, pending unban), assert `admin_actions_recent(10)` is empty and the stdout string is unchanged.
14. `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs`: add `("0095_moderation_audit.sql", "<checksum>"),` after the `0094` line, where `<checksum>` is the value the `every_migration_is_pinned...` failure output prints for the new file. Run no other migration edit: `0080` stays checksum-pinned.

## Tests

- `crates/server/tests/store/moderate.rs`: existing `moderate_commands::ban_is_idempotent_and_refuses_an_unknown_profile`, `unban_restores_a_banned_account_and_refuses_a_pending_one`, `revoke_round_trips_a_minted_code_and_is_idempotent`, `revoke_refuses_malformed_and_unknown_codes`, `redemption_round_trips_with_prior_state_lines`, extended with the row/no-row assertions above. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store moderate`.
- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, new `moderate_audit::memory::moderate_lever_routes_round_trip_with_null_actor` and `memory::moderate_route_guard_stays_an_allow_list` (plus their `postgres::` twins, skipped without `DATABASE_URL`): assert the exact rows and refusals above. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store moderate_audit` and `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store dev_dashboard` (the old R3074000 case must stay green against the `Option` change).
- `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs`: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store migrations_pinned`.
- Checks: `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p jackioh-server` (fake suite); the `sql` suite (`sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`, needs Docker) and `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Each lever writes exactly one row with the specified route and before/after when it changes something, in the same transaction; rows are visible via `GET /api/admin/audit` with `profileId ""`.
- [ ] Every listed no-op/refusal writes no row and prints today's line unchanged.
- [ ] No row carries an invite code in plaintext, only the stored hash.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, clippy, fmt, the pinned-checksum tests and the `sql` suite pass; no `#[ignore]`/`allow`/weakening used.

## Risks

- `NewAdminAction.profile_id: String` to `Option<String>` touches every constructor: only `api/admin.rs::audit()` and the contract helper build one (verified by grep), and `get_audit`/`remove_admin_rows` already handle `None`. The Postgres `postgres::` twin of the new contract case proves the NULL bind.
- SQL regex vs Rust allow-list drifting apart: both list the same four literals from `MODERATE_AUDIT_ROUTES`; the contract allow-list case pins the Rust side, the unchanged `46_dev_dashboard.sql` refused-list plus the new migration pin the SQL side.
- `set_redemption`/`revoke` idempotent paths share the commit: the append sits strictly inside the `revoked`/`previous != enabled` branch so a retry writes nothing new.

## Open questions

None. The NULL-actor decision and the no-ruling-note call are settled by the task; `apps/admin` and `spec/` need no change.
```
